criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: Introduction clearly states coral-reef monitoring need, one-spacecraft rationale and likely government/science users, with references. However operator/customer distinction is vague and citations are poor.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Thus, only one satellite is required.
The proposed satellite would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM) for research and/or education.

criteria.name: Main body: mission design - Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate - Include relevant screenshots and software files (in the main body of the report and/or appendix) - Include the following information: • Where it will launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? • What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? • Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? • Which ground control facilities will you use? • How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? • How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Covers launch, orbit, ground station and EOL with STK access evidence and orbital elements, but lacks payload/swath/link calculations and software files, and contains conceptual errors on RAAN, sunlight and equatorial launch.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Required sections and headings are present and readable, but figures/tables are unnumbered, bibliography uses bare URLs and Wikipedia, formatting and spelling are inconsistent.

evidence.quote: STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Report states equatorial launch maximises rotational velocity; this applies to prograde orbits, not retrograde SSO, so Kourou choice is not justified.
Initial RAAN 27.33° is described as indicating launch facility location; RAAN is an inertial node angle, not a ground-site coordinate.
Text says very high altitude yields low resolution images which is also desirable; for fluid-lensing reef imaging low resolution is undesirable.
Assumes descending passes are constantly sunlit; SSO is continuously sunlit only for dawn-dusk LTAN, which is not specified.
No sensor FOV, ground sample distance, swath or data-rate calculation supports 600 km altitude or 250 km reef coverage.
Selects Mt Pleasant radio observatory without showing compatible comms band, antenna gain, link budget or data rate; radio astronomy suitability unproven.
Access table has access 6 start/stop spanning about a day but duration 365 s, and access 15 duplicates access 14; access results need checking.
EOL section says satellite has no thrusters, yet orbit section calls EOL an orbital manoeuvre; passive drag sail is not a manoeuvre.
Drag-sail deorbit from 600 km not sized or timed; no demonstration of 25-year rule or complete burn-up.
No orbit maintenance or drag analysis over five-year life; replacement plan is generic.
Uses Wikipedia [6] as a source and lists bare URLs/malformed entries, contrary to referencing requirements.
Figures and tables lack figure/table numbers and full captions, so cross-referencing is incomplete.

overall: A readable preliminary design with adequate introduction and STK access work, but main design lacks payload/swath/link/EOL calculations and contains conceptual errors; referencing and figure/table labelling are inadequate.

feedback.summary: A readable preliminary design with a clear Introduction and useful STK access work. The main design is Adequate but lacks payload, swath, link-budget and EOL calculations, and contains conceptual errors on launch, RAAN and sunlight. Referencing and figure/table labelling need work. The Conclusion is generic. Use the next steps to add quantitative evidence, correct the design statements, and professionalise presentation.
next_steps: Add supporting calculations for sensor FOV/GSD/swath/data rate, a link budget for Mt Pleasant, and drag-sail deorbit sizing; correct the launch, RAAN and sunlight statements.
Number and caption every figure and table (e.g., Image 1), and replace Wikipedia/bare URLs with properly formatted references that match in-text citations.
Revise the Conclusion to include specific orbital/contact values and mission duration/EOL outcomes rather than generic claims.

criteria.C1: Your Introduction clearly establishes the coral-reef monitoring need, the one-spacecraft rationale and likely government/science users, with references. To strengthen within Accomplished, sharpen the operator versus customer distinction and improve citation quality; the current references are thin. Keep the mission purpose and user discussion as detailed as your opening paragraphs.
criteria.C2: You cover launch, orbit, ground station and EOL with STK access evidence and orbital elements, which is a solid Adequate base. To reach Accomplished, add payload/swath/link/EOL calculations and software files, and correct the launch, RAAN and sunlight statements. Support the 600 km altitude and 250 km reef coverage with sensor FOV, GSD, swath and data-rate evidence, and check the access table inconsistencies.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion summarises launch, orbit and ground station, but it is generic and omits mission duration/EOL and specific orbital/contact values. To reach Accomplished, tie conclusions directly to your evidence: state the chosen orbit and key elements, average contact duration, five-year life and drag-sail EOL outcome. Avoid broad claims like 'fully described satellite configuration' unless the report substantiates them.
criteria.C4: Your report has clear headings and is readable, but figures/tables are unnumbered and uncaptioned (e.g., Image 1), and the Bibliography includes Wikipedia and bare URLs. To reach Accomplished, use consistent engineering-report formatting, number and caption every figure/table, and cite properly formatted sources that match in-text citations. Check spelling and formatting consistency throughout.
